title: Unimodality conjecture for Toda eigenfunction numerators
statement:
For $\alpha\in Q^{\geq 0}$, let $\mathfrak{J}_\alpha$ be the Toda eigenfunction and let $(q)_\alpha$ be the associated $q$-factorial. A polynomial is **unimodal** if its coefficient sequence weakly increases to a maximum and then weakly decreases. **Unimodality conjecture.** The polynomial

$$
(q)_\alpha^2\mathfrak{J}_\alpha
$$

is unimodal. This is motivated by empirical observations after the positivity conjecture; the source gives no proof or resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10655

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).
source_name: Antoine Labelle, “On a specialization of Toda eigenfunctions”, arXiv:2502.10655 (2026).

progress.label: Open
progress.tldr: The conjecture remains unproved: experiments support it, but the proposed geometric route depends on another unproved conjecture.
progress.summary:
A. Labelle formulates the conjecture for every nonnegative root-lattice element: the numerator $(q)_\alpha^2\mathfrak{J}_\alpha$ should have coefficients that rise and then fall. The paper records empirical support but gives no general proof or resolution.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.10655)*

**Known results**

- In type $A$, unimodality would follow from Labelle's Conjecture 6.1, which predicts a smooth projective variety with the relevant Poincare polynomial; this implication is conditional.
- Positivity in type $A$ is established by Labelle's Theorem 1.2, but positivity in general remains conjectural.


Current status (as of August 2026): The conjecture is recorded and empirically supported, but no proof, verified counterexample, or resolution of general unimodality is reported.

*Caveats. No independent source corroborates a claimed counterexample or proof.*

solutions.body:
**Counterexample: the conjecture fails in every non-simply-laced irreducible Dynkin type.**

The exact current statement is Conjecture 7.3 of [A. Labelle, arXiv:2502.10655v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10655), revised July 28, 2026. It asserts unimodality of
\[
P_\alpha(q)=(q)_\alpha^2\mathfrak J_\alpha(q)
\]
for every nonnegative root-lattice element of an arbitrary split semisimple root system.

Write
\[
d_i=\frac{(\alpha_i,\alpha_i)}2,
\qquad
D_a=\prod_i(q^{d_i};q^{d_i})_{a_i},
\qquad
Q(a)=\frac12\left(\sum_i a_i\alpha_i,\sum_i a_i\alpha_i\right).
\]
The source's defining recursion is
\[
(1-q^{Q(a)})\mathfrak J_a
=
\sum_{\substack{0\le b\le a\\b\ne a}}
\frac{q^{Q(b)}}{D_{a-b}}\mathfrak J_b,
\qquad
\mathfrak J_0=1.
\tag{1}
\]
Substituting \(P_b=D_b^2\mathfrak J_b\) gives the exact integral triangular recurrence
\[
(1-q^{Q(a)})P_a
=
\sum_{\substack{0\le b\le a\\b\ne a}}
q^{Q(b)}P_b
\prod_i
\left[
\binom{a_i}{b_i}_{q^{d_i}}
\prod_{j=b_i+1}^{a_i}(1-q^{d_i j})
\right].
\tag{2}
\]

Now take type \(B_2\), ordering the long root first. Then
\[
(d_1,d_2)=(2,1),
\qquad
\bigl((\alpha_i,\alpha_j)\bigr)
=
\begin{pmatrix}4&-2\\-2&2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
Q(a,b)=2a^2-2ab+b^2.
\]
Applying (2) gives the complete small-index table
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
 &b=0&b=1&b=2\\ \hline
a=0&1&1&1\\
a=1&1&1+q+q^2&1+q+3q^2+q^3+q^4\\
a=2&1&1+q+q^2+q^3+q^4&
1+q+3q^2+2q^3+5q^4+2q^5+3q^6+q^7+q^8 .
\end{array}
\]
In particular, for \(\alpha=2\alpha_1+2\alpha_2\),
\[
\boxed{
P_\alpha(q)
=
1+q+3q^2+2q^3+5q^4+2q^5+3q^6+q^7+q^8.
}
\]
Every coefficient is strictly positive, and the polynomial is palindromic, but
\[
[q^2]P_\alpha=3>
[q^3]P_\alpha=2<
[q^4]P_\alpha=5.
\]
Hence \(P_\alpha\) is not unimodal.

The obstruction extends to every doubly-laced irreducible type. If a coefficient \(a_i=0\), every \(b\le a\) in (1) also has \(b_i=0\); thus the recursion depends only on the full Dynkin subdiagram supporting \(a\). Each \(B_r,C_r\) for \(r\ge2\), and \(F_4\), contains a \(B_2=C_2\) double-edge subdiagram. Put coefficient \(2\) on its two vertices and \(0\) elsewhere to obtain exactly the same nonunimodal polynomial.

For the remaining non-simply-laced type \(G_2\), take
\[
(d_1,d_2)=(1,3),
\qquad
Q(a,b)=a^2-3ab+3b^2,
\qquad
\alpha=3\alpha_1+3\alpha_2.
\]
The exact coefficient sequence from (2) is
\[
(1,2,5,11,16,24,39,46,60,84,88,99,119,110,
110,119,99,88,84,60,46,39,24,16,11,5,2,1).
\]
It again has positive full support and is palindromic, but contains
\[
119>110=110<119.
\]

Thus Conjecture 7.3 is false in every non-simply-laced irreducible Dynkin type. The separate simply-laced and type-\(A\) questions are not claimed here.
